answer: The quill multiplier is published, charged in dawn, and vine lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4801 identities would post 2000 proofs and burn roughly 55 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
